analysis.title: US Equities Mid-Day Color (GS Equities Mid-Day Color, 6 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Equities reverted higher at midday on 6 Nov 2026 (NDX > RTY > SPX) after a whipsaw week. SPX is just above its 200dma and over 60% of its constituents are down on the day.
The NFP print came in at 165k vs 70k expected. VIX is 'normalizing' to a 25-handle after its largest 1-day change since Covid. WTI is down slightly, below $90.

NDX is up 1.3% after its worst day since 3/9/20. GSPRHIMO (High Beta Momo) is up 2.4% after closing down 6.2% and finishing 51% below its June highs. SOX is up 3% after its worst day since 2020 and closed 14% below its 200dma.
GS TMT flow shows a lack of conviction and muted activity. Flows are more balanced than yesterday, with some dip buying in smaller notional size.

Prime brokerage: Global Fundamental L/S managers fell 1.3% yesterday (a -2SD move) on beta exposure. GS Prime flows show more hedging through Macro Products but no sign of panic or accelerated degrossing. 7/11 sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Consumer Discretionary and Industrials.
SPX Top of Book liquidity averaged $4mm yesterday, one of the least liquid sessions in four years, and was $3mm today. ETF volumes are 35% of the tape today vs 32% yesterday and a 28% YTD average.
CTAs are expected to be significant sellers of SPX and NDX over the next week: a combined $30mn in a flat tape, $22.3mn in an up tape and $31.2mm in a down tape.

GS franchise activity is 5 out of 10, with overall flows skewed 6.6% better to buy. LOs are 7.6% better to buy (communication services, industrials, info tech). HFs are 7.8% better to buy (macro products, info tech, energy). Info tech demand is on track to break a 6-day sell streak.

Chart of the Day: ETFs had their third-largest notional volume day in GS's dataset yesterday at $580bn, 33% of the broader tape. Levered ETFs took in a record $3bn and inverse ETFs saw a record -$2bn of outflows.
